title: On the Expressive Power of Permutation-Equivariant Weight-Space Networks
anchored_claims: Theorem 5.2 proves that the prominent permutation-equivariant weight-space architectures DWS, NP-NFN, HNP-NFN, GMN, and NG-GNN have identical expressive power for both invariant and equivariant mappings on compact sets (Theorem 5.2).

Proposition 5.3 shows Neural Functional Transformers (NFTs) differ in expressive power from the other architectures in general, but become equivalent under a general-position (GP) assumption requiring distinct bias terms per layer (Proposition 5.3).

Theorem 6.1 establishes that permutation-invariant weight-space networks are universal approximators of function-space functionals, i.e., maps depending only on the realized function and not the specific parameterization (Theorem 6.1).

Proposition 6.2 proves a non-universality result showing invariant weight-space networks cannot approximate all permutation-invariant functionals, using a counterexample built from Weisfeiler-Leman graph indistinguishability (Proposition 6.2).
Theorem 6.3 recovers universality for permutation-invariant functionals under the general-position assumption via continuous canonization maps that order neurons by bias value (Theorem 6.3).

Theorem 7.4 shows permutation-equivariant operators achieve universal approximation under the general-position assumption via canonization-based factorization, while Proposition 7.1 shows fixed-architecture equivariant networks cannot approximate function-space operators that increase geometric complexity (Proposition 7.1, Theorem 7.4).
